title: Prepared meals
question: How do you pick prepared meals?
decision: Hot food held hot and cold food held cold.
why: Hot buffet food is held at 140°F or above, and cold items below 40°F.
short_answer: Hot food in the case should sit at 140°F or above, and cold food below 40°F. Look for a thermometer facing out, and pans filled no higher than the rim.
detail: Hot buffet items belong in chafing dishes, slow cookers or warming trays at 140°F or above. Cold items like cut fruit and salads sit below 40°F, in bowls over ice. All buffet food is meant to be thrown out after two hours, whatever the holding temperature. An outward-facing thermometer shows the temperature inside the case. Pans piled into mounds above the rim cannot hold an even temperature. A sneeze guard should cover the food, and each dish should have its own utensil. Rotisserie chicken has a card of its own.
kristy_take: One food writer’s advice: skip late-night hot bar visits, when food is more likely to have sat a long time.
cart_pick: A dish from a case with a thermometer
buying_tips: Find the thermometer facing out and read it before choosing.
Pick pans filled to the rim, not piled into mounds.
Look for a sneeze guard and a separate utensil for each dish.
At home, two hours out at most, then into the fridge.
watch_out: Buffet food is thrown out after two hours, whatever the holding temperature.
tier_note: A thermometer facing out lets anyone read the case.
asked_as: which prepared meals should i buy
_do_line: Check the case thermometer, and pans filled no higher than the rim.
